Macrons

Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

ourselves pronoun

also we ourselves, by ourselves

classical

Cic. Att. 1.6.2: ut nōbīsmet ipsīs … placeāmus

nōs, nōbīs (reflexive)

pronoun: the ordinary forms of nōs, used reflexively

ourselves (as object)

No separate reflexive; stressed, nōsmet, nōbīsmet, usually with ipsī. “Each other” among us is inter nōs.

Other words

  • ipsī, ipsae, ipsa — ourselves (for emphasis: we ourselves)

    pronoun, intensive (plural of ipse) · classical · Cic. Fam. 4.14: sī nōsmet ipsōs regere possumus (Lewis & Short, s.v. agō)

    Agrees with nōs as subject (id nōsmet ipsōs facere oportet stresses us as the doers) or as object.

Examples

  • nōs Tusculānō ita dēlectāmur ut nōbīsmet ipsīs tum dēnique cum illō vēnimus placeāmus

    We love Tusculum so much that we are only pleased with ourselves when we have got there.Cic. Att. 1.6.2

  • Id nōsmet ipsōs facere oportet, Phaedria.

    We have to do it ourselves, Phaedria.Ter. Ph. 1.4.45 (Lewis & Short)

  • cāriōrem esse patriam nōbīs quam nōsmet ipsōs

    that our country is dearer to us than our own selvesCic. Fin. 3.19.64 (Lewis & Short)

  • agitur praeclārē, sī nōsmet ipsōs regere possumus

    we do very well if we can govern ourselvesCic. Fam. 4.14 (Lewis & Short)

  • ut nōsmet ipsī inter nōs conjūnctiōrēs sīmus

    so that we ourselves may be closer to each otherCic. Att. 14.13B.5 (Lewis & Short)

See also we, myself, yourselves, each other.

SourcesLewis & Short: nos · Lewis & Short: ipse

Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-cicero-epistulae), checked against the editions named there.

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
